transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-12-03
Time: 2:00 PM PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (AE), Maya Chen (SE), Rafael Gomez (Partner CS), Priya Nair (GTM) - Redwood; Samir Patel, Leah Ortiz, Tom Becker, Nina Alvarez - Aurora Partners

Summary: quick pipeline review and alignment on two priority co-sell opportunities, confirm roles, ask for technical benchmarks for the larger deal, and agree next steps for enablement & resource commitments. Some audio / auto-transcription noise, names occasionally mis-typed.

00:00 Jordan Lee: okay hey everyone thanks for joining, um this is Jordan from Redwood, i'll do a quick 5 minute agenda then hand over to Maya for the tech bits 00:12 Samir Patel: hey jordan, thanks, appreciate it 00:18 Leah Ortiz: hi all 00:22 Jordan Lee: quick agenda - review the partner pipeline, figure out who owns what for the two priority deals (fintech account and healthcare pilot), confirm security + procurement asks, and lay out next steps for co-sell support 00:36 Priya Nair: sounds good 00:40 Tom Becker: fine by me 00:44 Maya Chen: i'll cover quick runtime capabilities and what we need for the benchmarks 00:50 Rafael Gomez: and i'll share partner enablement items and our expectations for collateral 01:02 Jordan Lee: cool, samir you want to kick off with the pipeline brief? 01:07 Samir Patel: yeah so we have about six active leads, two of them are high priority - one is a mid-market fintech with expected ACV ~180k, the other is a regional healthcare provider pilot estimated 120k. the fintech is interested in a hosted api but wants strict data retention and audit logs, the healthcare one needs vpc/private deployment and pki/HSM alignment 01:35 Leah Ortiz: procurement on their side will push for SOC 2 plus ISO if we go deeper, also they asked about contractual SLAs 01:46 Nina Alvarez: and an internal security review will want RBAC detail and KMS integration 01:52 Jordan Lee: yep totally expected, we have a partner security one-pager and can add the SOC 2 attestation. we'll share those in the drive 02:04 Maya Chen: for the fintech workload we need sample prompt sets and traffic patterns, sequence lengths - that will determine recommended batching and quant profiles. also want to note that latency targets will affect whether hosted or dedicated is the right fit 02:20 Samir Patel: question - can Redwood guarantee <200ms p95 on the fintech traffic? that's their ask 02:27 Maya Chen: depends, um, if it's small prompts with short sequences we can hit that with hosted with our low-latency tier, but with larger contexts you'll want dedicated or pinned capacity. there's tradeoffs on cost 02:40 Tom Becker: any rough numbers for cost delta between hosted low-latency tier and dedicated? 02:46 Maya Chen: rough rule of thumb - dedicated reduces per-token cost by about 20-40% for steady throughput but adds commit costs; hosted is pay-as-you-go but can be 30-60% higher per token for sustained volume 03:01 Jordan Lee: and for co-sell alignment we can offer up to two weeks of pro-bono benchmark support for qualified deals to validate latency/cost 03:12 Samir Patel: that would help, especially for the fintech customer to see real numbers 03:17 Rafael Gomez: we'll need an ask from Aurora on accounts prioritized and their readiness level - i.e. are they procurement-ready, do they have security questionnaires ready, etc. 03:30 Leah Ortiz: for the healthcare pilot they already have a procurement window early q1 and need a VPC deployment inside the region - data residency concerns 03:40 Maya Chen: for VPC/private we have a checklist: network peering, allowed CIDRs, egress rules, and KMS/HSM setup. sometimes customers confuse KV cache with KV cache - or the transcriber will call it KV cash - but what we really need is to understand their session caching patterns 03:56 Tom Becker: (laughs) yep i've seen the KV cash typo 04:00 Jordan Lee: competitors - they mentioned VertexAI and CloudEndpointX doing similar pitches; Aurora thinks VertexAI is strong on enterprise integrations 04:10 Samir Patel: VertexAI offered a full bundle but they had questions on inference cost and on-prem options 04:18 Maya Chen: we should highlight Redwood's unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private and the rollout policies - it helps with graceful degradation and fallbacks during high load 04:28 Samir Patel: also curious - do you have references for healthcare private deployments? data residency is a hard ask 04:36 Jordan Lee: yes we have a reference in the EU with a regional bank and another healthcare pilot, we can share redacted case studies and an anonymized SLA summary 04:48 Nina Alvarez: procurement will want to see indemnity language and standard security annex; can we get that before legal review begins 04:55 Jordan Lee: yes, i'll drop our standard security annex and SOC 2 report link 05:00 Rafael Gomez: on co-sell enablement, partner portal will host the co-sell playbooks and joint collateral - i'll add Aurora to the portal and share the enablement deck 05:10 Samir Patel: great. on deal support who will be our main point? 05:15 Jordan Lee: i'll be the AE owner for both deals, maya will own technical validation, rafael will own partner enablement and partner ops, priya can help on pricing approvals 05:27 Leah Ortiz: procurement will need pre-sales estimates for TCO, do you have a template? 05:33 Maya Chen: yes we use a benchmarking template, i'll run the fintech scenario and share the latency/cost estimate - will need their sample prompts and expected qps 05:45 Samir Patel: i'll send the sample prompts and a redacted traffic profile by friday 05:50 Tom Becker: ok one technical ask - for the healthcare pilot, they want to know about audit logs retention and whether logs can be routed to their SIEM 05:58 Maya Chen: yes audit logs can be forwarded via syslog/S3 to customer buckets and we support configurable retention; we'll list the supported SIEM integrations in the doc 06:08 Jordan Lee: also note for private deployments we support customer-managed KMS and can surface HSM integration details 06:15 Nina Alvarez: good to hear, any changes to pricing for private deployments? 06:20 Jordan Lee: private has a platform fee plus support tier, and the on-prem option has additional setup fees; we'll put high level numbers in the spreadsheet 06:30 Rafael Gomez: ok let's walk through the two priority deals briefly - fintech (Deal A): status: qualification, estimated close q1, ask: two-week benchmark, data retention + SOC 2, likely hosted low-latency or dedicated depending on results 06:46 Samir Patel: notes: customer wants clear rollback plan in case of regressions, can we do canary and auto fallback? 06:53 Maya Chen: yes rollout policies support canary and automatic fallback to a cheaper compatible model if latency spikes 07:02 Leah Ortiz: healthcare pilot (Deal B): status: procurement request in early q1, need VPC deployment, KMS/HSM, and audit log routing 07:12 Jordan Lee: action - Aurora to prioritize accounts and send readiness matrix; Redwood to provide security docs, enablement deck, and run benchmarks 07:20 Samir Patel: can you also share a one pager for executives summarizing joint value prop? that's helpful for our sales leadership 07:27 Jordan Lee: yes we'll prepare a co-sell exec one-pager 07:32 Rafael Gomez: and i'm adding a shared spreadsheet link now - partner_deals_spreadsheet_v2.xlsx (shared link: https://drive.redwood.ai/partners/partner_deals_spreadsheet_v2) 07:48 Tom Becker: perfect 07:50 Jordan Lee: any blockers from Aurora's side? 07:53 Samir Patel: timeline is tight but manageable, procurement review may push a couple weeks; legal review timing depends on indemnity language 08:03 Nina Alvarez: we will escalate SOC 2 artifact requests internally 08:06 Maya Chen: technical note - when you send the sample workload please include typical sequence lengths, tokenization assumptions, and any system prompts; otherwise our latency estimates can be off 08:20 Leah Ortiz: noted 08:23 Jordan Lee: recap - Jordan to share security annex, SOC 2 link, co-sell one-pager, and enablement deck by 2025-12-05. Maya to run benchmarks and cost latency estimates by 2025-12-08. Samir to send sample prompts and accounts list by 2025-12-04. Rafael to add Aurora to partner portal and share spreadsheet access now 08:48 Samir Patel: thanks all, this was productive 08:52 Jordan Lee: thanks everyone, we'll get those artifacts over and follow up with scheduling 08:58 Meeting end

Notes on transcript quality: some speaker attribution is generic; minor transcription errors (Redwood sometimes spelled Redwoood, KV cache mis-heard as KV cash).
